title: Embeddings run only in the resident process; without it DD is inactive
trigger: when adding embeddings, vector search or any model runtime to DD retrieval
behavior_delta: Load embedding models only in the resident DD process (src/resident.js), never in a hook process. Store vectors in the SQLite index, not an external vector store. Without a resident whose model is loaded, DD is inactive and says so; lexical-only retrieval (DD_RETRIEVAL=lexical) exists for tests and evaluation, not as a user-facing fallback. Keep trigger activation, applicability gates and abstention; embeddings widen candidates and add a calibrated activation fused with the full-text ranking.
what: Load embedding models only in the resident DD process (src/resident.js), never in a hook process. Store vectors in the SQLite index, not an external vector store. Without a resident whose model is loaded, DD is inactive and says so; lexical-only retrieval (DD_RETRIEVAL=lexical) exists for tests and evaluation, not as a user-facing fallback. Keep trigger activation, applicability gates and abstention; embeddings widen candidates and add a calibrated activation fused with the full-text ranking.
why: An in-process ONNX runtime (@huggingface/transformers) measured 0.5 s cached load and 3 ms per query, so it cannot run per hook (L1) but works in a long-lived process; on the supermem benchmark semantic retrieval beat lexical on every metric. The previous version kept lexical retrieval as the fallback; L2 in docs/architecture/plugin-constraints.md now makes the resident required, and src/hooks/session-start.js keeps lexical mode for tests and evaluation only.
trigger_variants: Ajustar el floor semantico (semantic floor) o la calibracion de los embeddings
Cambiar como se calculan los embeddings

evidence_refs.summary: L2: one resident per machine; without it DD is inactive (never blocking) and says why.
lexicalMode(): DD_RETRIEVAL=lexical, for tests and evaluation; otherwise DD is inactive until the resident's model is ready.
Semantic activation calibrated against the query's mean similarity (floor 0.035).
